**My top pick for RV boondocking under $1,000 is the BLUETTI AC200L**, particularly if you want to power your RV through a dedicated 30A connection.

Based on the supplied 2026 search results, it offers a compelling combination of 2kWh battery capacity, high inverter output, and RV-specific connectivity.

    </row>

## How it compares

| Model | Capacity | Output | Reported price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $854.05 with code |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | $999 |
| EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $999 |
| Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 | 1,024Wh | 2,000W | $699 |

The Jackery is a good alternative if portability matters: its reported weight is 43.5 lb. The EcoFlow is also worth considering for solar charging. The Anker C1000 Gen 2 makes sense for shorter trips with lighter energy demands. <Link url="https://volt-vanguard.com/article/portable-power-station-for-rv/" title="RV comparison"/> · <Link url="https://sunenergytechnology.com/blog/best-portable-power-station-under-1000.html" title="Under-$1,000 comparison"/>

## What matters for boondocking

A 2kWh station is substantially more practical than a 1kWh model for running a compressor fridge, lights, electronics, and occasional appliances. However, usable AC energy will be lower than the advertised battery capacity because of inverter losses.

A 2kWh station generally isn't enough for sustained RV air conditioning. And although the AC200L has a TT-30 outlet, its 2,400W output does not provide the full 3,600W available from a conventional 30A RV hookup.

**Bottom line:** I'd choose the BLUETTI AC200L at the reported $854.05 price for its capacity, output, and RV outlet. Before buying, confirm the coupon, warranty, stock, and charging compatibility. The supplied results also note that the AC200L is an older model, which makes after-sales support worth checking.
